    READ & INTERPRET

    Which English option is closest?

    These are real cosine similarities to the source sentence, not accuracy percentages. The highest score wins this game; an embedding model can still miss a translation error.

    How the game decides

    ARC’s gpt-oss-120b writes a sentence in your chosen language and four English options. Their order is shuffled. Qwen3-Embedding-4B embeds all five texts; JavaScript calculates the cosine similarity between the source-language vector and each English vector.

    No model-generated score or answer key decides the winner. The highest cosine score earns a point. Scores within 0.000001 of the maximum count as a tie, and either tied answer earns a point. Display rounding can make different scores look equal.

    Scores stay hidden in the interface until you choose. This is a practice game, not a secure exam: browser developer tools can inspect the data. Similarity is not a guarantee of grammatical or semantic correctness.

    Your key stays in page memory and goes only to ARC. Session scores reset when the page reloads. Each round uses two API requests. A1–C2 are classroom targets for topics, vocabulary, and grammar—not certified proficiency assessments. Topics are sampled from the selected level’s group. Ancient Greek and Latin use analogous historical situations. The level does not manipulate embedding scores or trigger extra candidate rounds. About ARC’s API.
